attribute_fields.COMMENTS: Calculates State and Local Tax (SALT) deduction per IRC §164(b)(6)(B). For 2025-2028 OBBBA raised the cap from $10,000 (TCJA) to $40,000 with a phase-out: MAGI above $500,000 reduces the cap by 30% per dollar over the threshold, floored at $10,000 once MAGI hits $600,000. This top-level table is now a simple dispatcher: it resets intermediate fields, sums all SALT components into result.total_salt_collected via two helper tables (Sum_Primary_Residence_Tax over job.properties, Sum_SALT_Deduction over job.deductions), computes the effective cap via Calculate_Effective_SALT_Cap, then picks min(collected, cap) and adds it to result.total_itemized.

initial_action.initial_action_dsl: set result.salt_deduction = 0; set result.total_salt_collected = 0; set result.effective_salt_cap = 0; perform Sum_Primary_Residence_Tax; perform Sum_SALT_Deduction; perform Calculate_Effective_SALT_Cap
initial_action.initial_action_postfix: 0 cvd /result.salt_deduction xdef 0 cvd /result.total_salt_collected xdef 0 cvd /result.effective_salt_cap xdef /Sum_Primary_Residence_Tax performtable /Sum_SALT_Deduction performtable /Calculate_Effective_SALT_Cap performtable

action_details.action_comment: Cap binds -- limit deduction to the effective cap and log per IRC 164(b)(6)(B)
action_details.action_dsl: set result.salt_deduction = result.effective_salt_cap; set result.total_itemized = result.total_itemized + result.effective_salt_cap; add " SALT (capped): $" + result.salt_deduction + " (collected $" + result.total_salt_collected + ", effective cap $" + result.effective_salt_cap + ") per IRC 164(b)(6)(B)" to job.audit_trail
action_details.action_postfix: result.effective_salt_cap cvd /result.salt_deduction xdef result.total_itemized result.effective_salt_cap f+ cvd /result.total_itemized xdef " SALT (capped): $" result.salt_deduction strconcat " (collected $" strconcat result.total_salt_collected strconcat ", effective cap $" strconcat result.effective_salt_cap strconcat ") per IRC 164(b)(6)(B)" strconcat job.audit_trail swap addto

attribute_fields.COMMENTS: Calculates credit for taxes paid to other states to prevent double taxation. When a resident of one state (e.g., NY) earns income in another state (e.g., NJ), they pay tax to both states. The resident state provides a credit equal to the LESSER of: (a) tax actually paid to the other state, or (b) resident state tax on that same income. This prevents double taxation while ensuring the resident state collects at least its share.
